title: Derived adjunction of a ringed sequence projection
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ an inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings. Write $\mathscr S(B)$ for strict semilinear systems of module sheaves, with componentwise exactness, identified with modules over $B$ on the sequence site $\mathcal T=\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with compatible maps $A\to B_n$. Let $p:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)$ have inverse image on underlying sheaves the constant sequence, with ring map given by $A\to B_n$. The functors $Lp^*:D(A)\to D(\mathscr S(B))$ and $Rp_*:D(\mathscr S(B))\to D(A)$ exist and form a canonical adjunction. Its Hom bijection is the derived fraction extension of the ordinary correspondence $h:P\to p_*N\mapsto(x\otimes b\mapsto b\pi_nh(x))_n$. For one flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], $Lp^*P$ is represented by the strict complex $(Q\otimes_A B_n)_n$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], naturally in derived $P$. Ordinary direct image is $p_*N=\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B_n}N_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Tags 0941 (section-derived-limits before lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change) and 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); application to the ringed sequence projection.

proof.text: At level n use the existing normalized SystemScalarModel for A to B_n. Define the extension transition by transposing the unit at m through the sectionwise restriction-composition isomorphism. The pure-tensor transpose formula gives b tensor x mapped to rho(b) tensor x. Equality on local unit tensors proves the identity and composition laws and compatibility with maps of A-modules. Exact evaluation detects the additive structure.

Restrict each N_n along A to B_n. Apply scalar restriction to each strict transition and compose with the canonical restriction-composition isomorphism, whose section maps are identities. This gives an inverse diagram in A-modules, functorially in N. Define F as its categorical limit and pi_n as its projections. The cone equations give compatibility on sections; every compatible family is a cone and the limit lift gives the full existence and uniqueness assertion.

The level scalar Hom equivalences send each strict map G(M) to N to a compatible cone M to Res N_n. Conversely a map M to F(N) transposes each projection to a level map. Generator extensionality and the transition formula prove strict compatibility. The limit universal property and the scalar equivalence inverse identities prove the two composites are identities. Naturality gives the ordinary adjunction. Its normalized tensor formula is b times pi_n(h(x)); additivity of its left adjoint makes its right adjoint additive.

Resolve every base complex by one flat-term K-flat complex using the independent-coefficient K-flat resolution theorem. The scalar cochain models preserve quasi-isomorphisms between these representatives at every level, hence componentwise detection proves the whole extension does so. Pass the class to the homotopy category and apply the resolving-class left-derived theorem. Transfer its universal comparison through the homotopy quotient to complexes. The comparison is invertible on every representative in this class. For q:Q to P define c as the inverse of L([q]) followed by epsilon_Q; its required equation follows from the inverse laws.

The strict-system category is Grothendieck abelian through its equivalence with the ringed sequence site at the coefficient universe. Its K-injective resolutions give the universal right derived pair of F by CategoryTheory.exists_derived, with the comparison invertible on every K-injective complex.

Apply derivedAdjunctionOfResolvingClass to the ordinary adjunction, the resolving class and its preservation result, and the universal left and right pairs. Its normalized Hom equation is exactly the asserted equation on every chain map, after replacing the homotopy comparison with its equal cochain component. This normalization extends along all inverted quasi-isomorphisms, without requiring a chosen representative to represent every derived map by a chain map.
